title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 6. Wandering in the Southern Country
html:
The Lord travels towards Purushottama: Tamolipta; Remuna, where Gopinatha lets His crown fall to Him; the river Vaitarani; Yajapura (Jajpur) with the Boar, Viraja, Nabhi-Gaya and countless lingas of Shiva

Verse 1

इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ देवो हरिकीर्तनतत्परः।
पथस्था देवता दृष्ट्वा नत्वा स्तुत्वा यथाविधि॥१॥

ityuktvā prayayau devo harikīrtanatatparaḥ|
pathasthā devatā dṛṣṭvā natvā stutvā yathāvidhi||1||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; prayayau — set out; devah — the Lord; hari-kirtana-tatparah — intent on chanting the name of Hari; patha-sthah — standing by the road; devatah — deities; drishtva — seeing; natva — bowing; stutva — praising; yatha-vidhi — as is proper.

1So saying, the Lord set out again, wholly intent on chanting the name of Hari; whenever He saw the deities standing by the road, He bowed to them and offered praises, as is proper.

Verse 2

तमोलिप्ते महापुण्ये हरेः क्षेत्रे जगद्गुरुः।
ब्रह्मकुण्डे कृतस्नानो ददर्श मधुसूदनम्॥२॥

tamolipte mahāpuṇye hareḥ kṣetre jagadguruḥ|
brahmakuṇḍe kṛtasnāno dadarśa madhusūdanam||2||

tamolipte — at Tamolipta; maha-punye — most holy; hareh — of Hari; kshetre — in the sacred abode; jagat-guruh — the Guru of the world; brahma-kunde — in the Brahma-kunda; krita-snanah — having bathed; dadarsha — beheld; madhusudanam — Madhusudana.

2At Tamolipta1, the most holy abode of Hari, the Teacher of the world bathed in the Brahma-kunda and beheld Madhusudana.

Verse 3

ततो जगाम भगवान्दिनैः कतिपयैः प्रभुः।
रेमुणायां महापुर्यां द्रष्टुं गोपालदेवकम्॥३॥

tato jagāma bhagavāndinaiḥ katipayaiḥ prabhuḥ|
remuṇāyāṁ mahāpuryāṁ draṣṭuṁ gopāladevakam||3||

tatah — then; jagama — came; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dinaih — in days; katipayaih — a few; prabhuh — the Lord; remunayam — to Remuna; maha-puryam — the great town; drashtum — to see; gopala-devakam — the Lord Gopala (the Deity).

3Then, within a few days, Bhagavan, the Lord, came to the great town of Remuna to see the Lord Gopala —

Verse 4

वाराणस्यामुद्धवेन स्थापितं पूजितं पुरा।
ब्राह्मणानुग्रहार्थाय तत्र गत्वा स्थितं हरिम्॥४॥

vārāṇasyāmuddhavena sthāpitaṁ pūjitaṁ purā|
brāhmaṇānugrahārthāya tatra gatvā sthitaṁ harim||4||

varanasyam — in Varanasi; uddhavena — by Uddhava; sthapitam — installed; pujitam — worshipped; pura — of old; brahmana-anugraha-arthaya — to show favour to a brahmana; tatra — there; gatva — having gone; sthitam — abiding; harim — Hari.

4that Hari who of old was installed and worshipped by Uddhava in Varanasi, and who, to show favour to a brahmana, went there and remained2.

Verse 5

गोपीनाथमिति केचिदाहुस्तं करुणानिधिम्।
क्षीरचौरादिलीलां यश्चकार भक्तहेतवे॥५॥

gopīnāthamiti kecidāhustaṁ karuṇānidhim|
kṣīracaurādilīlāṁ yaścakāra bhaktahetave||5||

gopinatham — Gopinatha; iti — thus; kechit — some; ahuh — call; tam — Him; karuna-nidhim — the treasury of mercy; kshira-chaura-adi-lilam — the pastime of the thief of sweet rice and others; yah — who; chakara — performed; bhakta-hetave — for the sake of a devotee.

5Some call that treasury of mercy Gopinatha: for the sake of His devotee He performed the pastime of the thief of sweet rice, and others besides3.

Verse 6

सर्वं प्रमाणमेवात्र भक्तवाक्यानुगो हरिः।
ददर्श तत्र गत्वासौ भगवान्प्राकृतो यथा॥६॥

sarvaṁ pramāṇamevātra bhaktavākyānugo hariḥ|
dadarśa tatra gatvāsau bhagavānprākṛto yathā||6||

sarvam — everything; pramanam — proof; eva — indeed; atra — here; bhakta-vakya-anugah — who follows the words of His devotees; harih — Hari; dadarsha — beheld; tatra — there; gatva — going; asau — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; prakritah yatha — like an ordinary man.

6Everything here bears witness that Hari follows the words of His devotees. Bhagavan went there and, like an ordinary man, beheld Him.

Verse 7

दण्डवद्भुवि निपत्य सुरेशं
तं प्रणम्य करुणार्द्रमुखेन्दुः।
नर्तनं निजजनैः सह चक्रे
कीर्तनं सरसिजायतनेत्रः॥७॥

daṇḍavadbhuvi nipatya sureśaṁ
taṁ praṇamya karuṇārdramukhenduḥ|
nartanaṁ nijajanaiḥ saha cakre
kīrtanaṁ sarasijāyatanetraḥ||7||

danda-vat — like a staff; bhuvi — on the ground; nipatya — falling; sura-isham — to the Lord of the gods; tam — that; pranamya — bowing; karuna-ardra-mukha-induh — His moon-face moist with compassion; nartanam — dancing; nija-janaih saha — with His own; chakre — performed; kirtanam — kirtana; sarasija-ayata-netrah — His eyes long like lotuses.

7Falling to the ground like a staff, He bowed to the Lord of the gods; His moon-face grew moist with compassion, and He, whose eyes are long like lotuses, danced with His own and sang kirtana.

Verse 8

तत्क्षणान्मुररिपोः प्रतिमाया
मौलिलग्नमुकुटं च समाप।
तदवलोक्य करपद्मयुगेन
तद्दधार श्रीशचीसुत एषः॥८॥

tatkṣaṇānmuraripoḥ pratimāyā
maulilagnamukuṭaṁ ca samāpa|
tadavalokya karapadmayugena
taddadhāra śrīśacīsuta eṣaḥ||8||

tat-kshanat — at that very moment; mura-ripoh — of the Enemy of Mura; pratimayah — of the image; mauli-lagna-mukutam — the crown fixed on the head; cha — and; samapa — reached (Him); tat — that; avalokya — seeing; kara-padma-yugena — with His two lotus hands; tat — it; dadhara — caught; shri-shachi-sutah — the son of Sri Shachi; eshah — He.

8And at that very moment the crown fixed on the head of the Deity of the Enemy of Mura fell right to Him. Seeing this, the son of Sri Shachi caught it in His two lotus hands.

Verse 9

तत्प्रसादमधिगत्य स्वमूर्ध्ना
सन्दधार च रराज च हृष्टः।
अद्भुतं तमवलोक्य सुरेशं
खे ननन्द नतकन्धरचित्तः॥९॥

tatprasādamadhigatya svamūrdhnā
sandadhāra ca rarāja ca hṛṣṭaḥ|
adbhutaṁ tamavalokya sureśaṁ
khe nananda natakandharacittaḥ||9||

tat-prasadam — that grace; adhigatya — receiving; sva-murdhna — on His own head; sandadhara — placed; cha — and; raraja — shone; cha — and; hrishtah — joyful; adbhutam — wondrous; tam — that; avalokya — beholding; sura-isham — Lord of the gods; khe — in the inner space (of the heart); nananda — rejoiced; nata-kandhara-chittah — with bowed neck and heart.

9Receiving that grace, He placed the crown on His own head and shone with joy; and, beholding the wondrous Lord of the gods, He rejoiced in the depths of His heart4, with bowed head and soul.

Verse 10

तत्र नृत्यमकरोदतुलश्री-
र्न्यासिनां वरः सुधाकरकान्तिः।
वैष्णवैः सह दिनान्तरमन्तः
सायमेव विरराम महात्मा॥१०॥

tatra nṛtyamakarodatulaśrī-
rnyāsināṁ varaḥ sudhākarakāntiḥ|
vaiṣṇavaiḥ saha dināntaramantaḥ
sāyameva virarāma mahātmā||10||

tatra — there; nrityam akarot — danced; atula-shrih — of peerless beauty; nyasinam — of sannyasis; varah — the best; sudhakara-kantih — radiant as the moon; vaishnavaih saha — with the Vaishnavas; dina-antaram antah — all through the day; sayam eva — only in the evening; virarama — stopped; maha-atma — the great soul.

10And there He of peerless beauty, the best of sannyasis, radiant as the moon, danced with the Vaishnavas all through the day, and only in the evening did the great soul stop.

Verse 11

तं विलोक्य मुदिता जनसङ्घा-
स्तुष्टुवुर्मुहुरमुं प्रशशंसुः।
तत्र सोऽपि रजनीं प्रणिनाय
भक्ष्यमन्नमुपभोज्य मुनीशः॥११॥

taṁ vilokya muditā janasaṅghā-
stuṣṭuvurmuhuramuṁ praśaśaṁsuḥ|
tatra so'pi rajanīṁ praṇināya
bhakṣyamannamupabhojya munīśaḥ||11||

tam — Him; vilokya — seeing; mudita — delighted; jana-sanghah — the crowds of people; tushtuvuh — hymned; muhuh — again and again; amum — Him; prashashamsuh — praised; tatra — there; sah — He; api — and; rajanim — the night; praninaya — spent; bhakshyam annam — food to eat; upabhojya — having partaken of; muni-ishah — the lord of sages.

11Seeing Him, the crowds of people rejoiced and hymned and praised Him again and again. And the lord of sages, having partaken of the food offered, spent the night there.

Verse 12

प्रातरम्बुजमुखः स जगाम
देशमन्यनगराणि लङ्घयन्।
प्राप्य कालमनु कम्बुसुकण्ठो
वेगिनीं सुरनदीझरच्युताम्॥१२॥

prātarambujamukhaḥ sa jagāma
deśamanyanagarāṇi laṅghayan|
prāpya kālamanu kambusukaṇṭho
veginīṁ suranadījharacyutām||12||

pratah — in the morning; ambuja-mukhah — lotus-faced; sah — He; jagama — went on; desham — the country; anya-nagarani — other towns; langhayan — passing by; prapya — reaching; kalam anu — in time; kambu-su-kanthah — His lovely neck like a conch; veginim — the swift (river); sura-nadi-jhara-chyutam — flowing down from the stream of the river of the gods.

12In the morning the lotus-faced Lord, whose lovely neck is like a conch, went on, passing through the country and other towns, and in time He reached a swift river flowing down from the stream of the river of the gods —

Verse 13

तां विलोक्य वरवैतरणीं स
सर्वपातककुलं जनतायाः।
दर्शनेन यमवैतरणी सा
जातु भाति किमु तत्स्नपनेन॥१३॥

tāṁ vilokya varavaitaraṇīṁ sa
sarvapātakakulaṁ janatāyāḥ|
darśanena yamavaitaraṇī sā
jātu bhāti kimu tatsnapanena||13||

tam — that; vilokya — seeing; vara-vaitaranim — the excellent Vaitarani; sah — He; sarva-pataka-kulam — the whole host of sins; janatayah — of the people; darshanena — by the sight (of her); yama-vaitarani — Yama's Vaitarani; sa — that; jatu — ever; bhati — appears; kim u — how much less; tat-snapanena — by bathing in her.

13the excellent Vaitarani5, which washes away the whole host of people's sins. Whoever sees her will never face the Vaitarani of Yama — how much less one who bathes in her!

Verse 14

स्नानमत्र विधिना स विधाय
तं ददर्श वरशूकररूपम्।
यस्य दर्शनवशान्मनुजानां
सप्तसप्ततिकुलं दिवमीयात्॥१४॥

snānamatra vidhinā sa vidhāya
taṁ dadarśa varaśūkararūpam|
yasya darśanavaśānmanujānāṁ
saptasaptatikulaṁ divamīyāt||14||

snanam — bath; atra — here; vidhina — according to rule; sah — He; vidhaya — taking; tam — Him; dadarsha — beheld; vara-shukara-rupam — in the form of the excellent Boar; yasya — whose; darshana-vashat — by virtue of the sight; manujanam — of men; sapta-saptati-kulam — seventy-seven generations; divam — to heaven; iyat — go.

14Having bathed here according to the rule, He beheld the Lord in the form of the excellent Boar: by virtue of the sight of Him seventy-seven generations of a man's line go to heaven.

Verse 15

तं विलोक्य मुदितः स जगाम
याजपुरनामनगरीं द्विजभूमिम्।
यत्र यज्ञमकरोच्चतुर्मुखः
शासनं द्विजवराय ददौ च॥१५॥

taṁ vilokya muditaḥ sa jagāma
yājapuranāmanagarīṁ dvijabhūmim|
yatra yajñamakaroccaturmukhaḥ
śāsanaṁ dvijavarāya dadau ca||15||

tam — Him; vilokya — beholding; muditah — delighted; sah — He; jagama — came; yajapura-nama-nagarim — to the town called Yajapura; dvija-bhumim — the land of brahmanas; yatra — where; yajnam — a sacrifice; akarot — performed; chatur-mukhah — the Four-faced; shasanam — a grant of land; dvija-varaya — to the best of brahmanas; dadau — gave; cha — and.

15Having seen Him, He came joyfully to the town called Yajapura6, the land of brahmanas, where the Four-faced one performed a sacrifice and granted land to the best of brahmanas.

Verse 16

यत्र मृत्युमधिगम्य तु विश्वाः
पापिनोऽपि शिवरूपधराः स्युः।
तत्र लिङ्गशतशो हि समीक्ष्य
शङ्करस्य शिरसानमदीशः॥१६॥

yatra mṛtyumadhigamya tu viśvāḥ
pāpino'pi śivarūpadharāḥ syuḥ|
tatra liṅgaśataśo hi samīkṣya
śaṅkarasya śirasānamadīśaḥ||16||

yatra — where; mrityum — death; adhigamya — meeting; tu — indeed; vishvah — all; papinah — sinners; api — even; shiva-rupa-dharah — bearing the form of Shiva; syuh — become; tatra — there; linga-shatashah — lingas by the hundred; hi — indeed; samikshya — seeing; shankarasya — of Shankara; shirasa — with His head; anamat — bowed; ishah — the Lord.

16Those who die there, even sinners, take on the form of Shiva. Seeing there the lingas of Shankara by the hundred, the Lord bowed His head to them.

Verse 17

स जगाम विरजामुखपद्म-
दर्शनाय भगवान्करुणाब्धिः।
यां विलोक्य जगतां जनुकोटि-
मात्रमघं ह्यखिलं प्रजहाति॥१७॥

sa jagāma virajāmukhapadma-
darśanāya bhagavānkaruṇābdhiḥ|
yāṁ vilokya jagatāṁ janukoṭi-
mātramaghaṁ hyakhilaṁ prajahāti||17||

sah — He; jagama — went; viraja-mukha-padma-darshanaya — to see the lotus face of Viraja; bhagavan — Bhagavan; karuna-abdhih — the ocean of mercy; yam — whom; vilokya — on seeing; jagatam — of people; janu-koti-matram — amassed over millions of births; agham — sin; hi — indeed; akhilam — all; prajahati — departs.

17Bhagavan, the ocean of mercy, went to see the lotus face of Viraja7; whoever beholds her is freed from all the sins amassed over millions of births.

Verse 18

तां विलोक्य प्रणमन्समयाचत्
प्रेमभक्तिमतुलां जगदीशः।
आजगाम गयनाभिमनर्घ्यं
पैत्रतीर्थमरविन्दमुखेशः॥१८॥

tāṁ vilokya praṇamansamayācat
premabhaktimatulāṁ jagadīśaḥ|
ājagāma gayanābhimanarghyaṁ
paitratīrthamaravindamukheśaḥ||18||

tam — her; vilokya — seeing; pranaman — bowing; samayachat — begged for; prema-bhaktim — devotion in love; atulam — peerless; jagat-ishah — the Lord of the world; ajagama — came; gaya-nabhim — to Gaya-nabhi; anarghyam — priceless; paitra-tirtham — the holy place for the rites of the ancestors; aravinda-mukha-ishah — the lotus-faced Lord.

18Seeing her, the Lord of the world bowed down and begged for peerless loving devotion. Then the lotus-faced Lord came to priceless Gaya-nabhi8, the holy place for the rites of the ancestors.

Verse 19

ब्रह्मकुण्डपयसि द्विजवर्यः
स्नानमाशु विदधे विधानवित्।
यत्र यज्ञवराहप्रकाश-
दर्शनेन जगतां सुखमासीत्॥१९॥

brahmakuṇḍapayasi dvijavaryaḥ
snānamāśu vidadhe vidhānavit|
yatra yajñavarāhaprakāśa-
darśanena jagatāṁ sukhamāsīt||19||

brahma-kunda-payasi — in the waters of the Brahma-kunda; dvija-varyah — the best of brahmanas; snanam — bath; ashu — at once; vidadhe — took; vidhana-vit — knowing the injunctions; yatra — where; yajna-varaha-prakasha-darshanena — by the sight of the manifestation of Yajna-Varaha; jagatam — to the worlds; sukham — happiness; asit — came.

19The best of brahmanas, versed in the injunctions, at once bathed in the waters of the Brahma-kunda, where the manifestation of Yajna-Varaha9, appearing to view, brought happiness to the worlds.

Verse 20

बभ्राम तत्र भगवान्नगरीं निरीक्ष्य
भूतेशलिङ्गमवलोक्य महानुभावः।
वाराणसीमिव सदाशिवराजधानीं
यत्र त्रिलोचनमुखाः शिवलिङ्गकोटिः॥२०॥

babhrāma tatra bhagavānnagarīṁ nirīkṣya
bhūteśaliṅgamavalokya mahānubhāvaḥ|
vārāṇasīmiva sadāśivarājadhānīṁ
yatra trilocanamukhāḥ śivaliṅgakoṭiḥ||20||

babhrama — wandered; tatra — there; bhagavan — Bhagavan; nagarim — the town; nirikshya — viewing; bhuta-isha-lingam — the linga of the Lord of beings; avalokya — beholding; maha-anubhavah — the great-souled; varanasim — Varanasi; iva — like; sadashiva-rajadhanim — the capital of Sadashiva; yatra — where; trilochana-mukhah — headed by Trilochana; shiva-linga-kotih — millions of Shiva lingas.

20The great-souled Bhagavan wandered there, viewing the town and beholding the linga of the Lord of beings: the town is like Varanasi, the capital of Sadashiva, where there are millions of Shiva lingas headed by Trilochana10.

Verse 21

श्रुत्वा हरेरिदमनन्तसुखं लभेत
पुण्यां कथां सकलपापहरां मनुष्यः।
तीर्थाटनस्य च फलं पितृतीर्थसर्व-
यज्ञक्रियाफलमशेषगुणान्वितः स्यात्॥२१॥

śrutvā hareridamanantasukhaṁ labheta
puṇyāṁ kathāṁ sakalapāpaharāṁ manuṣyaḥ|
tīrthāṭanasya ca phalaṁ pitṛtīrthasarva-
yajñakriyāphalamaśeṣaguṇānvitaḥ syāt||21||

shrutva — having heard; hareh — of Hari; idam — this; ananta-sukham — endless happiness; labheta — will gain; punyam — holy; katham — account; sakala-papa-haram — that takes away all sins; manushyah — a man; tirtha-atanasya — of pilgrimage; cha — and; phalam — the fruit; pitri-tirtha-sarva-yajna-kriya-phalam — the fruit of all sacrificial rites at the holy places of the ancestors; ashesha-guna-anvitah — endowed with every virtue; syat — will become.

21Whoever hears this holy account of Hari, which takes away all sins, will gain endless happiness, the fruit of pilgrimage and the fruit of all sacrificial rites at the holy places of the ancestors, and will be endowed with every virtue.

Thus ends the sixth sarga, "Wandering in the Southern Country" (Dakshinadesha-bhramana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Tamolipta (Tamralipta), an ancient port town in south-western Bengal (present-day Tamluk).
  2. All the witnesses read "in Varanasi". Cf. the legend of the Deity Gopala who followed a brahmana in order to bear witness to the word given him.
  3. Gopinatha of Remuna is known as Kshirachora, "the Thief of Sweet Rice": He hid a pot of sweet rice for His devotee Madhavendra Puri.
  4. Literally "in space"; understood as the space of the heart. The reading is doubtful.
  5. The Vaitarani is a river in Orissa; a river of the same name in the realm of Yama, the god of death, bars sinners from the other world.
  6. Yajapura ("City of the Sacrifice"), present-day Jajpur in Orissa.
  7. Viraja is the goddess worshipped at Yajapura.
  8. Gaya-nabhi (Nabhi-Gaya), a holy place in Yajapura where, according to legend, lies the navel of the demon Gaya; here, as at Gaya, rites for the ancestors are performed.
  9. Yajna-Varaha, the Boar who is the embodiment of sacrifice (Vishnu as Varaha).
  10. Trilochana ("the Three-eyed"), one of the principal lingas of Shiva in Varanasi.
